theorems.MCCCCXVII: There are exactly 84 Clifford fibrations: partitions of the 120 vertices of the 600-cell into 12 pairwise vertex-disjoint great decagons
theorems.MCCCCXVIII: The 84 fibrations split into 12 special (degree 5 in the fibration-disjointness graph) and 72 generic (degree 25)
theorems.MCCCCXIX: The 12 special fibrations form the disconnected graph K_6 ⊔ K_6: two disjoint complete graphs on 6 vertices each
theorems.MCCCCXX: The two K_6 components are the LEFT-Clifford family L = {L_0,...,L_5} and the RIGHT-Clifford family R = {R_0,...,R_5}; each independently partitions all 72 great decagons
theorems.MCCCCXXI: Each (L_i, R_j) pair shares exactly 2 decagons; the 36 cross-pairs tile all 72 decagons exactly once
theorems.MCCCCXXII: The 36 (L_i,R_j) cross-pairs biject with the 36 spreads of W(3,3); the boson/fermion coset split is geometrically encoded as L/R Clifford chirality
theorems.MCCCCXXIII: There are exactly 122 = 2 × 61 ways to partition all 72 decagons into 6 fibrations of 12; exactly 2 of these use only special fibrations
theorems.MCCCCXXIV: Antipodal vertices (v, -v) of the 600-cell share identical Clifford (L,R) addresses; the Clifford coordinate system is naturally defined on the antipodal quotient
theorems.MCCCCXXV: There are exactly 60 unique (L,R) Clifford addresses, one per antipodal pair of the 600-cell
theorems.MCCCCXXVI: The 12 special fibrations = 6 left + 6 right = the two icosahedral chiral families of Clifford translations on S^3
theorems.MCCCCXXVII: The 72 generic fibrations form a 25-regular disjointness graph; 25 = 5^2 = Phi_5^2
theorems.MCCCCXXVIII: The count 72 is self-dual: there are 72 great decagons AND 72 generic fibrations; each generic fibration corresponds to exactly one great decagon
theorems.MCCCCXXIX: 122 = 2 × 61 where 61 is prime; the 2 canonical fibration-partitions are the L-partition and R-partition; the 120 non-canonical ones arise from mixing L and R fibers
theorems.MCCCCXXX: The L × R sharing matrix is the uniform all-2 matrix: every L_i shares exactly 2 decagons with every R_j, expressing perfect symplectic exchange symmetry
theorems.MCCCCXXXI: 84 = 72 + 12: the generic fibration count equals the decagon count (self-dual); the 12 special fibrations are the chiral residue
theorems.MCCCCXXXII: Master fibration theorem: 72 great decagons → 12 special Clifford fibrations → K_6 ⊔ K_6 = L ∪ R, with L × R ↔ 36 W(3,3) spreads; the 600-cell's Clifford structure is the geometric realization of W(3,3)'s symplectic spread structure
